parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the probability that either all three own an electric car or none of them owns an electric car.

A random sample of 125 of the residents of Wimfield is selected.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Use a suitable approximation to find the probability that more than 45 of these residents own an
electric car.

text: 30% of the residents of Wimfield own an electric car. Three residents are chosen at random.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Draw up the probability distribution table for X.

text: A red fair six-sided dice has faces labelled 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2. A blue fair six-sided dice has faces labelled
1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3. Both dice are thrown. The random variable X is the product of the scores on the two dice.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the probability that a randomly chosen adult male in Molimba has a height greater than
170 cm. 
60% of adult males in Molimba have a height between 170 cm and k cm, where k is greater than 170.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the value of k, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Draw a cumulative frequency graph to illustrate the data.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use your graph to estimate the 30th percentile of the heights of the sunflower plants.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Calculate estimates for the mean and the standard deviation of the heights of the 150 sunflower
plants.

text: On a certain day, the heights of 150 sunflower plants grown by children at a local school are measured,
correct to the nearest cm. These heights are summarised in the following table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the probability that she obtains no more than 2 chocolates that are wrapped in red foil. 
Jake chooses chocolates one at a time at random from the production line.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the probability that the first time he obtains a chocolate that is wrapped in red foil is before
the 7th choice. 
Keifa chooses chocolates one at a time at random from the production line.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Find the probability that the second chocolate chosen is the first one wrapped in gold foil given
that the fifth chocolate chosen is the first unwrapped chocolate.

text: A factory produces chocolates. 30% of the chocolates are wrapped in gold foil, 25% are wrapped in red
foil and the remainder are unwrapped.
Indigo chooses 8 chocolates at random from the production line.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements of the 9 letters in the word HAPPINESS.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the number of different arrangements of the 9 letters in the word HAPPINESS in which the
first and last letters are not the same as each other.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Find the number of different arrangements of the 9 letters in the word HAPPINESS in which the
two Ps are together and there are exactly two letters between the two Ss. 
The 9 letters in the word HAPPINESS are divided at random into a group of 5 and a group of 4.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Find the probability that both Ps are in one group and both Ss are in the other group.
